1: import { DEFAULT_SETTINGS, Settings, type ReqflowApi } from "@reqflow/core";
2: import { createStore } from "zustand/vanilla";
3: import { ReqflowError } from "./bridge-client";
4: 
5: /**
6:  * Where the settings live, as far as the UI knows:
7:  * - "loading": asking the main process
8:  * - "saved": loaded from / saved to disk
9:  * - "unavailable": main has no settings storage yet (WS1) — changes apply until the app restarts
10:  * - "error": loading or saving failed; `error` says why
11:  */
12: export type SettingsPersistence = "loading" | "saved" | "unavailable" | "error";
13: 
14: export interface SettingsState {
15:   settings: Settings;
16:   persistence: SettingsPersistence;
17:   error: string | null;
18:   /** Ask main for the stored settings. Keeps the defaults when storage isn't built yet. */
19:   load(): Promise<void>;
20:   /**
21:    * Merge `patch` into one section, validated with the `Settings` schema. Returns a readable
22:    * error and changes nothing when invalid; otherwise applies it and saves in the background.
23:    */
24:   update<K extends keyof Settings>(section: K, patch: Partial<Settings[K]>): string | null;
25:   resetSection(section: keyof Settings): void;
26: }
27: 
28: const SAVE_DELAY_MS = 400;
29: 
30: export function createSettingsStore(client: Pick<ReqflowApi, "settings">) {
31:   let saveTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
32: 
33:   return createStore<SettingsState>()((set, get) => {
34:     const save = () => {
35:       clearTimeout(saveTimer);
36:       saveTimer = setTimeout(async () => {
37:         if (get().persistence === "unavailable") return;
38:         try {
39:           const saved = await client.settings.save(get().settings);
40:           set({ settings: saved, persistence: "saved", error: null });
41:         } catch (err) {
42:           if (err instanceof ReqflowError && err.code === "not_implemented") {
43:             set({ persistence: "unavailable", error: null });
44:           } else {
45:             set({ persistence: "error", error: errorMessage(err, "Saving settings failed") });
46:           }
47:         }
48:       }, SAVE_DELAY_MS);
49:     };
50: 
51:     const apply = <K extends keyof Settings>(section: K, value: Settings[K]): string | null => {
52:       const parsed = Settings.shape[section].safeParse(value);
53:       if (!parsed.success) {
54:         const issue = parsed.error.issues[0];
55:         return issue ? issue.message : "Invalid value";
56:       }
57:       set({ settings: { ...get().settings, [section]: parsed.data } });
58:       save();
59:       return null;
60:     };
61: 
62:     return {
63:       settings: DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
64:       persistence: "loading",
65:       error: null,
66: 
67:       async load() {
68:         set({ persistence: "loading", error: null });
69:         try {
70:           const stored = Settings.parse(await client.settings.get());
71:           set({ settings: stored, persistence: "saved" });
72:         } catch (err) {
73:           if (err instanceof ReqflowError && err.code === "not_implemented") {
74:             set({ persistence: "unavailable" });
75:           } else {
76:             set({ persistence: "error", error: errorMessage(err, "Loading settings failed") });
77:           }
78:         }
79:       },
80: 
81:       update(section, patch) {
82:         return apply(section, { ...get().settings[section], ...patch });
83:       },
84: 
85:       resetSection(section) {
86:         apply(section, DEFAULT_SETTINGS[section]);
87:       },
88:     };
89:   });
90: }
91: 
92: function errorMessage(err: unknown, fallback: string): string {
93:   return err instanceof Error && err.message ? `${fallback}: ${err.message}` : fallback;
94: }

54:       const units = cost(url,opts.body);
55:       if (options.limits.maxProviderCredits && credits + units > options.limits.maxProviderCredits) throw new ProviderError("limit_reached", "Conservative provider-credit budget exhausted.");
56:       requests++; credits += units;
57:       let response: Response;
58:       try {
59:         response = await withAbort((options.fetchImpl ?? fetch)(url.href, {
60:           method, redirect:"error", signal:ownSignal,
61:           headers:{ ...(typeof opts.body === "string" ? {} : opts.body ? {"Content-Type":"application/json"}:{}), ...opts.headers },
62:           body: opts.body === undefined ? undefined : typeof opts.body === "string" ? opts.body : JSON.stringify(opts.body),
63:         }),ownSignal);
64:       } catch (error) {
65:         if (ownSignal.aborted) throw abortError(ownSignal);
66:         if (method === "GET" && attempt < options.limits.retries) { await delay(250*2**attempt,ownSignal); continue; }
67:         throw errorReport(error);
68:       }
69:       if (!response.ok) {
70:         const status = response.status;
71:         await response.body?.cancel();
72:         const retryAfter = response.headers.get("retry-after");
73:         const wait = retryAfter ? /^\d+(\.\d+)?$/.test(retryAfter) ? Number(retryAfter)*1000 : Math.max(0,Date.parse(retryAfter)-Date.now()) : 250*2**attempt;
74:         if (method === "GET" && (status===429 || status>=500) && attempt<options.limits.retries && Number.isFinite(wait) && wait<=30000) { await delay(wait,ownSignal); continue; }
75:         throw new ProviderError(status===401?"invalid_credentials":status===403?"permission_required":status===429||status===402?"rate_limited":"unreachable", `Provider HTTP ${status}.`,status);
76:       }
77:       if (Number(response.headers.get("content-length"))>16*1024*1024) { await response.body?.cancel(); throw new ProviderError("limit_reached","Provider response exceeds 16 MiB."); }
78:       const reader = response.body?.getReader();
79:       if (!reader) return "";
80:       const chunks:Uint8Array[]=[]; let size=0;
81:       try {
82:         for (;;) { const {done,value}=await withAbort(reader.read(),ownSignal); if(done)break; size+=value.byteLength; if(size>16*1024*1024) throw new ProviderError("limit_reached","Provider response exceeds 16 MiB."); chunks.push(value); }
83:       } finally { if (ownSignal.aborted || size>16*1024*1024) await reader.cancel().catch(()=>{}); reader.releaseLock(); }
84:       return Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8");
85:     }
86:   }
87:   async function request(value:string,opts:HttpOptions={}):Promise<string> {
88:     const url=new URL(value);
89:     if(url.protocol!=="https:"||url.username||url.password||url.port||!HOSTS.has(url.hostname)) throw new ProviderError("permission_required","Request endpoint is outside the fixed provider allowlist.");
90:     const ownSignal = opts.signal ? AbortSignal.any([signal,opts.signal]):signal;
91:     // In-run original-document reuse only; a new run has a fresh cache and never hides revisions.
92:     const cacheable = url.hostname==="api.firecrawl.dev" && url.pathname.endsWith("/scrape");
93:     const key=createHash("sha256").update(JSON.stringify([value,opts.body])).digest("hex");
94:     if(cacheable && cache.has(key)) return withAbort(cache.get(key)!,ownSignal);
95:     const work=(async()=>{await acquire();try{return await perform(url,opts,ownSignal);}finally{release();}})();
96:     if(cacheable) { cache.set(key,work); work.catch(()=>cache.delete(key)); }
97:     return work;
98:   }
99:   return {
100:     get requests(){return requests;}, text:request,
101:     async json<T>(url:string,opts?:HttpOptions):Promise<T> { const text=await request(url,opts); try{return JSON.parse(text) as T;}catch{throw new ProviderError("unreachable","Provider returned malformed JSON.");} },
102:   };
103: }

1: import {
2:   BLOCK_SPECS,

12:   removeEdges,
13:   renameBlock as renameInGraph,
14:   setBlockParams,
15:   updateGraphAt,
16:   type BlockParams,
17:   type Connection,
18:   type ConnectionCheck,
19:   type PaletteBlockKind,
20:   type WorkflowBlock,
21:   type WorkflowGraph,
22: } from "@reqflow/core";
23: import type { EdgeChange, NodeChange } from "@xyflow/react";
24: import { useStore } from "zustand";
25: import { createStore } from "zustand/vanilla";
26: 
27: /**
28:  * Editor state for the Data Flow page. The workflow is one tree of workplaces (`root`); `path`
29:  * says which inner workplace is open. All graph rules live in @reqflow/core (graph.ts) — this
30:  * store only applies them to the open workplace and turns errors into a visible notice.
31:  */
32: 
33: export type XY = { x: number; y: number };
34: /** A React Flow connection: handle ids are port ids. */
35: export type FlowConnection = {
36:   source: string | null;
37:   target: string | null;
38:   sourceHandle?: string | null;
39:   targetHandle?: string | null;
40: };
41: export interface Notice {
42:   id: number;
43:   tone: "info" | "error";
44:   message: string;
45: }
46: export interface Crumb {
47:   depth: number; // pass to goTo()
48:   label: string;
49: }
50: 
51: export interface DataflowState {
52:   root: WorkflowGraph;
53:   path: string[]; // ids of blocks whose inner workplaces are open, outermost first
54:   selectedBlockIds: string[];
55:   selectedEdgeIds: string[];
56:   measured: Record<string, { width: number; height: number }>; // React Flow sizes, by block id
57:   notice: Notice | null;
58: 
59:   /** Adds a block to the open workplace, selects it and returns its id. */
60:   addBlock(kind: PaletteBlockKind, position: XY): string;
61:   applyNodeChanges(changes: NodeChange[]): void;
62:   applyEdgeChanges(changes: EdgeChange[]): void;
63:   /** For React Flow's isValidConnection: same rules as connect(), without side effects. */
64:   checkConnection(connection: FlowConnection): ConnectionCheck;
65:   connect(connection: FlowConnection): boolean;
66:   /** Deletes the selected blocks (boundary blocks excluded) and edges. */
67:   deleteSelection(): void;
68:   /** Returns an error message, or null when applied. */
69:   setParams(blockId: string, params: BlockParams): string | null;
70:   renameBlock(blockId: string, label: string): string | null;
71:   selectBlock(blockId: string | null): void;
72:   openInner(blockId: string): void;
73:   goTo(depth: number): void;
74:   notify(tone: Notice["tone"], message: string): void;
75:   dismissNotice(): void;
76: }
77: 
78: /** Ids look like "ai-filter-3f9c1a2b": readable in logs, unique across the workflow. */
79: export function newBlockId(kind: PaletteBlockKind): string {
80:   return `${kind.replace(/_/g, "-")}-${crypto.randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`;
81: }
82: 
83: export function toCoreConnection(c: FlowConnection): Connection | null {
84:   if (!c.source || !c.target || !c.sourceHandle || !c.targetHandle) return null;
85:   return {
86:     source: c.source,
87:     sourcePort: c.sourceHandle,
88:     target: c.target,
89:     targetPort: c.targetHandle,
90:   };
91: }
92: 
93: /** Breadcrumb for the open workplace: "Workplace › Research › AI Filter". */
94: export function breadcrumbOf(root: WorkflowGraph, path: readonly string[]): Crumb[] {
95:   const crumbs: Crumb[] = [{ depth: 0, label: "Workplace" }];
96:   let graph = root;
97:   path.forEach((id, i) => {
98:     const block = graph.blocks.find((b) => b.id === id);
99:     crumbs.push({ depth: i + 1, label: block?.label ?? id });
100:     graph = block?.inner ?? emptyGraph();
101:   });
102:   return crumbs;
103: }
104: 
105: export const selectWorkplace = (s: DataflowState): WorkflowGraph => graphAt(s.root, s.path);
106: 
107: /** The block the inspector shows: exactly one selected block on the open workplace. */
108: export function selectInspectedBlock(s: DataflowState): WorkflowBlock | null {
109:   if (s.selectedBlockIds.length !== 1) return null;
110:   return selectWorkplace(s).blocks.find((b) => b.id === s.selectedBlockIds[0]) ?? null;
111: }
112: 
113: const message = (err: unknown) => (err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));
114: 
115: /** Readable first Zod issue, e.g. `Branches: Too small: expected array to have >=2 items`. */
116: function paramError(err: unknown, kind: WorkflowBlock["kind"]): string {
117:   const issues = (err as { issues?: { path: PropertyKey[]; message: string }[] }).issues;
118:   const issue = issues?.[0];
119:   if (!issue) return message(err);
120:   const key = String(issue.path[0] ?? "");
121:   const label = isBoundaryBlockKind(kind)
122:     ? key
123:     : (BLOCK_SPECS[kind].params.find((p) => p.key === key)?.label ?? key);
124:   return label ? `${label}: ${issue.message}` : issue.message;
125: }
126: 
127: export function createDataflowStore(initial: WorkflowGraph = emptyGraph()) {
128:   let noticeId = 0;
129: 
130:   return createStore<DataflowState>()((set, get) => {
131:     /** Runs `update` on the open workplace; on error, shows it and leaves the state unchanged. */
132:     const edit = (update: (graph: WorkflowGraph) => WorkflowGraph): boolean => {
133:       try {
134:         const current = selectWorkplace(get());
135:         const next = update(current);
136:         if (next !== current) set({ root: updateGraphAt(get().root, get().path, () => next) });
137:         return true;
138:       } catch (err) {
139:         get().notify("error", message(err));
140:         return false;
141:       }
142:     };
143: 
144:     return {
145:       root: initial,
146:       path: [],
147:       selectedBlockIds: [],
148:       selectedEdgeIds: [],
149:       measured: {},
150:       notice: null,
151: 
152:       addBlock(kind, position) {
153:         const id = newBlockId(kind);
154:         const label = nextBlockLabel(get().root, BLOCK_SPECS[kind].label);
155:         const block = createBlock(kind, { id, label, position });
156:         if (edit((g) => ({ ...g, blocks: [...g.blocks, block] }))) {
157:           set({ selectedBlockIds: [id], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
158:         }
159:         return id;
160:       },
161: 
162:       applyNodeChanges(changes) {
163:         let selected = new Set(get().selectedBlockIds);
164:         let measured = get().measured;
165:         const removed: string[] = [];
166:         const ok = edit((graph) => {
167:           let g = graph;
168:           for (const c of changes) {
169:             if (c.type === "position" && c.position) g = moveBlock(g, c.id, c.position);
170:             else if (c.type === "dimensions" && c.dimensions) {
171:               measured = { ...measured, [c.id]: c.dimensions };
172:             } else if (c.type === "select") {
173:               selected = new Set(selected);
174:               if (c.selected) selected.add(c.id);
175:               else selected.delete(c.id);
176:             } else if (c.type === "remove") removed.push(c.id);
177:           }
178:           return removed.length ? removeBlocks(g, removed) : g;
179:         });
180:         if (!ok) return;
181:         for (const id of removed) selected.delete(id);
182:         set({ selectedBlockIds: [...selected], measured });
183:       },
184: 
185:       applyEdgeChanges(changes) {
186:         let selected = new Set(get().selectedEdgeIds);
187:         const removed = changes.filter((c) => c.type === "remove").map((c) => c.id);
188:         for (const c of changes) {
189:           if (c.type !== "select") continue;
190:           selected = new Set(selected);
191:           if (c.selected) selected.add(c.id);
192:           else selected.delete(c.id);
193:         }
194:         if (removed.length && !edit((g) => removeEdges(g, removed))) return;
195:         for (const id of removed) selected.delete(id);
196:         set({ selectedEdgeIds: [...selected] });
197:       },
198: 
199:       checkConnection(connection) {
200:         const c = toCoreConnection(connection);
201:         if (!c) return { ok: false, reason: "Connect an output port to an input port." };
202:         return checkConnection(selectWorkplace(get()), c);
203:       },
204: 
205:       connect(connection) {
206:         const c = toCoreConnection(connection);
207:         if (!c) {
208:           get().notify("error", "Connect an output port to an input port.");
209:           return false;
210:         }
211:         return edit((g) => connectPorts(g, c));
212:       },
213: 
214:       deleteSelection() {
215:         const graph = selectWorkplace(get());
216:         const blocks = graph.blocks
217:           .filter((b) => get().selectedBlockIds.includes(b.id) && !isBoundaryBlockKind(b.kind))
218:           .map((b) => b.id);
219:         const edges = get().selectedEdgeIds;
220:         if (edit((g) => removeEdges(removeBlocks(g, blocks), edges))) {
221:           set({ selectedBlockIds: [], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
222:         }
223:       },
224: 
225:       setParams(blockId, params) {
226:         const graph = selectWorkplace(get());
227:         const block = graph.blocks.find((b) => b.id === blockId);
228:         if (!block) return `Block "${blockId}" is not on this workplace`;
229:         try {
230:           const result = setBlockParams(graph, blockId, params);
231:           set({ root: updateGraphAt(get().root, get().path, () => result.graph) });
232:           const n = result.removedEdges.length;
233:           if (n > 0) {
234:             get().notify(
235:               "info",
236:               `Removed ${n} connection${n === 1 ? "" : "s"} from ports that no longer exist.`,
237:             );
238:           }
239:           return null;
240:         } catch (err) {
241:           return paramError(err, block.kind);
242:         }
243:       },
244: 
245:       renameBlock(blockId, label) {
246:         try {
247:           const graph = renameInGraph(selectWorkplace(get()), blockId, label);
248:           set({ root: updateGraphAt(get().root, get().path, () => graph) });
249:           return null;
250:         } catch (err) {
251:           return message(err);
252:         }
253:       },
254: 
255:       selectBlock(blockId) {
256:         set({ selectedBlockIds: blockId ? [blockId] : [], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
257:       },
258: 
259:       openInner(blockId) {
260:         const block = selectWorkplace(get()).blocks.find((b) => b.id === blockId);
261:         if (!block?.inner) {
262:           get().notify("error", `"${block?.label ?? blockId}" has no inner workplace.`);
263:           return;
264:         }

1: # Generic workflow execution and research run controls
2: 
3: ## Scope and acceptance
4: 
5: This slice adds one generic executor to `@reqflow/engine` and exposes the existing run IPC contract
6: on the Data Flow page. It does not implement AI blocks, register blocks, construct research providers,
7: change shared schemas, persist data, or make human decisions. Those responsibilities remain in main
8: and the owning block implementations.
9: 
10: Acceptance is an offline run of a validated workflow graph with correct port routing, independent
11: branch preservation, boundary routing, cancellation, and resumable nested HIL pauses. The renderer
12: saves the root graph before starting, displays live run states and research collection limitations,
13: and delegates exports to the native main-process save dialog.
14: 
15: ## Engine API
16: 
17: ```ts
18: type WorkflowOutputs = Record<string, Record<string, PipelineData>>;
19: 
20: function executeWorkflow(options: {
21:   run: WorkflowRun;
22:   registry: BlockRegistry;
23:   context: (blockId: string) => BlockContext;
24:   outputs?: WorkflowOutputs;
25:   onUpdate: (run: WorkflowRun) => void | Promise<void>;
26: }): Promise<{ run: WorkflowRun; outputs: WorkflowOutputs }>;
27: ```
28: 
29: The function and named option/result/output types are exported from `@reqflow/engine`.
30: 
31: - `validateGraph` runs before contexts or updates. Invalid graphs reject immediately.
32: - Each workplace runs in stable topological order. Multiple incoming edges merge in graph edge order
33:   with `mergePipelineData`; later duplicate IDs win. Unconnected inputs receive empty envelopes.
34: - Inputs are cloned so an implementation cannot corrupt an earlier successful output by mutating its input.
35: - A Custom block always runs its inner workplace. Research and AI Filter use their registered builtin
36:   when their inner workplace has only untouched boundary blocks. An inner edge or non-boundary block
37:   overrides the builtin, including a direct input-to-output boundary connection.
38: - `block_input.out` carries its parent's named input. `block_output.in` becomes the parent's named
39:   output. Boundaries are engine-owned and do not require registry entries.
40: - A missing builtin fails that block with a clear registry error. Failed descendants are skipped;
41:   independent branches continue and keep their outputs. There are no placeholder AI implementations.
42: - Implementations must return exactly the output ports declared by `blockPorts`. Every envelope is
43:   schema-validated before publication. Validation preserves research provenance extensions instead
44:   of stripping extended record fields. Sink outputs are `{}`.
45: - Counts are computed from the deduplicated union of a block's output envelopes. Sinks have zero
46:   output counts. Builtin placeholder boundaries are explicitly skipped, not left pending.
47: - Only HIL implementations may return `paused`. Ancestors reflect `waiting_for_review`, dependent
48:   nodes remain pending, and independent branches may finish. If failure and review coexist, the run
49:   waits for review while retaining the failure; the final resumed run fails unless no branch failed.
50: - Terminal runs cannot be re-executed. Successful and failed blocks are not replayed when continuing.
51:   Only previously paused HIL receives `ctx.resumed = true`; newly reached HIL still pauses normally.
52: - Cancellation stops awaiting even an implementation that ignores its signal. Successful data stays
53:   available; unfinished states become skipped, and the run becomes cancelled. Late engine logs,
54:   progress, and results are ignored. Blocks must still obey their signal before external side effects:
55:   the executor cannot undo a provider request or database write performed by an uncooperative block.
56: - Log/progress callbacks preserve the supplied context callbacks and emit immutable run snapshots.
57:   Subscriber calls are serialized and awaited. Persistence/subscriber errors reject instead of being
58:   silently reported as successful execution.
59: 
60: ## Main-process integration requirements
61: 
62: There must be **no second orchestrator** in the IPC handlers. Main starts this executor in the
63: background and retains/observes its promise; `runs.start` returns the initial snapshot promptly.
64: 
65: 1. Register every builtin actually used by the selected workflow in `BlockRegistry`. A customized
66:    expandable subflow does not require that parent's builtin, but its inner leaf implementations do.
67: 2. Build `WorkflowRun` from the saved workflow version and graph/scope snapshot. Supply contexts
68:    with one shared run `AbortSignal`, settings snapshot, audit/files/LLM/car services, and `ctx.research`
69:    for the registered Research implementation. The executor does not construct a collector or resolve
70:    advanced research scope; the registered block and shared parameter contract own that behavior.
71: 3. Pass an explicit mutable `outputs` map. The executor writes a validated output before emitting its
72:    succeeded snapshot. `onUpdate` can persist the snapshot and newly succeeded outputs atomically,
73:    then push `IPC_EVENTS.runUpdate`. Persist all output maps, including `{}` for sinks and boundaries.
74:    Do not parse extended research records into a stripped-down persistence representation.
75: 4. Record run lifecycle audit events in main, based on actual status transitions. Blocks remain
76:    responsible for their domain audit events. The executor does not approve/reject/defer requirements.
77: 5. Retain one `AbortController` and active execution promise per run. `runs.cancel` aborts it and
78:    waits for the executor's final cancelled snapshot. To cancel a persisted paused run after its
79:    execution promise has settled, main must also persist a cancelled status or re-enter the executor
80:    with that paused snapshot and an already-aborted signal.
81: 6. `runs.resume` accepts a waiting run only, reloads the same graph and every successful block's
82:    persisted per-port outputs, applies already-audited human edits through main's existing review
83:    services, supplies a fresh non-aborted context signal, and calls this same executor. Missing stored
84:    successful outputs reject clearly; they are never silently rebuilt or replaced with empty data.
85: 7. Persist collector `ResearchDataset` results under the run ID before final run completion reaches
86:    the renderer. `research.dataset` should return successful and partial collections, including
87:    blocked/missing-credential outcomes with zero records. Keep these distinct from an absent dataset.
88: 8. Implement `exports.research({ runId, format })` for JSON, XLSX, and CSV with a native save dialog.
89:    Return `null` for dialog cancellation; surface real errors through the existing IPC error contract.
90: 
91: Because `onUpdate` receives only the run snapshot, main must use its explicit shared output map when
92: persisting per-port data during execution. Awaiting only the final result would lose outputs on an
93: application shutdown during human review.
94: 
95: ## Renderer behavior
96: 
97: Run controls save `dataflowStore.getState().root`, never the open inner workplace, as
98: `Research workflow` with Settings' `defaultScope`. Further runs reuse the saved workflow ID and let
99: main bump its version. Advanced scope remains a generic Research inspector parameter.
100: 
101: The controls subscribe before starting so fast pushed completion cannot be overwritten by a stale
102: `runs.start` response. Save/start/cancel/export have explicit busy flags and visible error states.
103: The latest workflow/run identity survives tab navigation for the current app session; remounting
104: refreshes that run through `runs.get`. The editor is still session-only on application restart.
105: This slice does not add a second workflow browser or autosave system.
106: 
107: An expandable last-run panel shows each non-boundary block's status, progress, output counts, errors,
108: and recent logs. Output inspection calls `runs.blockOutput` and limits the JSON preview to 20,000
109: characters. Completed, failed, and cancelled Research runs load `research.dataset` and display every
110: agent's status, record count, request count, and limitations. An unavailable dataset is an error,
111: not an empty result. Synthetic datasets are marked explicitly. JSON/XLSX/CSV exports include the full
112: dataset and remain main-process operations. Waiting runs link to Car review; controls never decide
113: requirements or automatically resume human review.
114: 
115: ## Offline verification
116: 
117: ```sh
118: npx vitest run packages/engine/src/executor.test.ts \
119:   apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/RunControls.test.ts
120: ```
121: 
122: Executor tests cover DAG ordering, merge/fan-out, splitter ports, invalid graphs/outputs, missing
123: implementations, independent failures, Research collector invocation, nested boundaries, builtin
124: fallback/override, nested and sequential HIL resume, missing resume data, cancellation, late result
125: suppression, progress/log snapshots, persistence errors, provenance preservation, and input isolation.
126: Run-control helper tests exercise save-before-start, root/scope/version reuse, invalid/offline errors,
127: stale-response handling, cancel behavior, distinct agent statuses, and native export IPC contracts.
128: 
129: Full main-process end-to-end research execution depends on the integration requirements above; the
130: helper tests deliberately use synthetic fixtures and never call a real research provider.
</content>

1: # Publication, statistics and local document collection
2: 
3: These adapters return provider-owned original records through the final `ProviderAdapter` contract.
4: They do not classify opinions with AI, infer preferences from statistics, create forecasts, approve
5: requirements, or execute instructions contained in collected documents. All filesystem and subprocess
6: operations belong in the Electron main process.
7: 
8: ## Exported factories and integration
9: 
10: ```ts
11: // packages/blocks/src/research/providers/openalex.ts
12: createOpenAlexAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
13: // packages/blocks/src/research/providers/eurostat.ts
14: createEurostatAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
15: // packages/blocks/src/research/providers/documents.ts
16: createLocalDocumentsAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
17: 
18: // packages/blocks/src/research/documents/local.ts
19: interface LocalDocumentReaderOptions {
20:   resolveFile: (id: string) => Promise<{ path: string; name: string }>;
21:   doclingCommand?: string;
22: }
23: createLocalDocumentReader(
24:   options: LocalDocumentReaderOptions,
25: ): NonNullable<ProviderContext["documents"]>
26: ```
27: 
28: The parent supplies `resolveFile` from its trusted imported-file store. Renderer inputs are imported
29: `file_…` IDs only; the renderer never supplies a path or executable. The resolver must return an
30: absolute path to a regular, non-symlink file. An executable setting is main-process configuration,
31: not a document or renderer instruction. Use an absolute executable path when it is outside `PATH`.
32: 
33: ```ts
34: const reader = createLocalDocumentReader({ resolveFile: (id) => importedFiles.resolve(id) });
35: // Supply this same reader through ProviderContext.documents for both BMW agents.
36: const documents = reader;
37: ```
38: 
39: Cache document reads **in the parent run**, keyed by imported file ID and page limit. Share an
40: in-flight promise between `bmw_sales` and `bmw_strategy` when both select the same imported ID.
41: Scope that cache to a run with a shared run abort signal, remove failed promises, and do not reuse
42: cancelled promises across runs. The reader deliberately does not maintain a persistent content cache.
43: This preserves original source/record IDs and lets the parent deduplicate records while retaining
44: both collecting-agent associations. Adapters neither infer an import's BMW dataset kind from its
45: filename nor independently count repeated sheet associations as opinions.
46: 
47: Source identity uses `reqflow-file:///<fileId>`, not `file://` URLs containing private user paths.
48: `sourceTitle` is the imported ID. `metadata.originalArtifact = { fileId }` points back to the parent
49: file store; temporary conversion artifacts are not source identities. Table sheet names, row numbers,
50: Docling JSON pointers, page numbers and bounding boxes remain available for evidence lookup.
51: 
52: ## OpenAlex
53: 
54: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
55: 
56: - [Search works](https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works).
57: - [Cursor pagination](https://docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api/get-lists-of-entities/paging).
58: - [Work attributes](https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/work-object).
59: - [Authentication](https://docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api/rate-limits-and-authentication).
60: 
61: Collection uses `GET https://api.openalex.org/works`, `search`, publication-date/language `filter`,
62: `cursor=*`, and response `meta.next_cursor`. Page size is at most the currently supported 100.
63: Queries come from the supplied query plan, scope questions, scope keywords, or vehicle/market scope;
64: no unrelated default research topic is substituted. Publication-date and supported two-letter
65: language filters come from scope. Geographic applicability is **not** inferred from author affiliation,
66: query wording, or a requested EU market. Allowed-domain rules cannot constrain OpenAlex's scholarly
67: corpus through these filters; this adapter collects OpenAlex metadata, not arbitrary linked sites.
68: 
69: Optional `openalex_api_key` travels only in the officially supported `Authorization: Bearer …`
70: header, never in a URL, output record, or adapter log. The injected HTTP transport must also redact
71: authorization headers. HTTP failures are converted to fixed, credential-safe messages. Pagination
72: deduplicates work IDs and reports result/request limits, repeated cursors, cancellation and partial
73: page failures explicitly. The connection probe performs one search with `per_page=1&select=id,title`.
74: 
75: `abstract_inverted_index` is reconstructed by position with original tokens and no paraphrasing.
76: Returned text is labeled `ABSTRACT\n…`; `metadata.contentLevel` is `abstract`. Missing or ambiguous
77: indexes yield explicitly labeled metadata-only records. Publication metadata includes title, DOI,
78: authors, bibliographic fields, date/year, language, work type, OA and retraction metadata.
79: 
80: An explicitly OA primary-location PDF URL is preserved only as an **unretrieved original reference**
81: with `accessibility: "provider_metadata"`. Credential-bearing links are not retained. This contract
82: has no remote binary downloader/parser, so this adapter does not download PDFs, scrape landing pages,
83: retrieve OpenAlex metered content, or call local Docling on remote documents. OpenAlex abstracts and
84: OA flags are **not full-text evidence** and do not provide complete commercial market studies.
85: 
86: ## Eurostat
87: 
88: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
89: 
90: - [Statistics API overview and time filters](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/user-guides/data-browser/api-data-access/api-getting-started/api).
91: - [Statistics API detailed guidelines](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/user-guides/data-browser/api-data-access/api-detailed-guidelines/api-statistics).
92: 
93: Collection requires explicit `scope.eurostatDatasets`, including dataset codes and dimension filters.
94: Without them, the outcome is `blocked` with a selection limitation, not unrelated statistics. Requests
95: use the official Statistics 1.0 JSON-stat 2.0 endpoint with `format=JSON` and an API-supported label
96: language (`EN`, `DE`, `FR`). Geographic filters are passed exactly; `EU` is never expanded to an EU
97: aggregate or country list. `time`/`time_period`, `sinceTimePeriod`, `untilTimePeriod` and
98: `lastTimePeriod` remain explicit dataset selections. Conflicting time modes and simultaneous
99: `geo`/`geoLevel` are rejected. Publication dates are not silently reinterpreted as observation periods.
100: 
101: Each dataset selection produces a raw metrics **table record**, not prose conclusions. Row-major
102: coordinate decoding follows `id` and `size`; both dimension codes and category labels appear in
103: columns. Values remain numeric, zero remains zero, and missing/suppressed observations remain `null`.
104: Observation status strings, including combined flags such as `ep`, are preserved without interpretation.
105: Dimensions, labels, explicit units, notes, annotations, raw sparse/dense values/status and full
106: extensions are retained. `updated` is dataset metadata, not an observation's publication date.
107: 
108: A selection is capped at 20,000 observation cells. Larger or asynchronous extractions produce an
109: explicit limitation requesting narrower filters; no partial table is mislabeled complete. Dataset
110: failures preserve successful preceding selections. The connection probe retrieves a single latest
111: `demo_pjan` observation for `geo=DE&sex=T&age=TOTAL`, not a research run or default dataset suggestion.
112: 
113: ## Local TXT and XLSX
114: 
115: Plain UTF-8 TXT is retained verbatim as one passage. Invalid encoding is rejected rather than
116: silently replacing bytes. Text is never interpreted as executable instructions.
117: 
118: Regular XLSX uses the existing `exceljs` dependency, with deterministic workbook/sheet order.
119: Every sheet is preserved; the first nonempty row is the header, subsequent row positions and values
120: remain exact, including interior blank rows and `null` cells. Empty header cells remain empty strings.
121: This deterministic header rule is stated as a limitation; it is not a semantic header detector.
122: Numbers, booleans, strings, saved formula results, rich text, hyperlink display text and ISO date
123: representations are supported. Formula objects, rich-text/hyperlink artifacts, date formats and cell
124: notes remain in metadata. Formulas, hyperlinks and macros are never executed or followed. Explicit
125: unit columns/header markers and source cell notes populate table units/footnotes. Units are not
126: inferred from a value's magnitude. `maxPages` does not truncate spreadsheet sheets.
127: 
128: The `Feedback_Explorer` layout requires explicit feedback ID, text and VFC columns. Repeated
129: **same ID + same text** rows become one `feedback` record with multiple original VFC associations,
130: row locators and source classifications. Different IDs remain distinct even with identical text;
131: different texts under one ID remain separate and carry a conflict limitation. Classification cells
132: are marked `origin: "source_explicit"`; no AI classification or additional independent opinion is
133: created. Conflicting market/vehicle cells remove single-value attribution but retain original rows.
134: 
135: Files are capped at 64 MiB, each sheet at 100,000 rows and 512 columns. These are fail-explicit safety
136: bounds, not silent truncation. Plain TXT and XLSX need no Python or Docling installation.
137: 
138: ## Optional local Docling subprocess
139: 
140: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
141: 
142: - [Installation](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/getting_started/installation/).
143: - [CLI reference](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/reference/cli/).
144: - [Model prefetch and offline usage](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/advanced_options/).
145: 
146: PDF/DOCX/PPTX conversion is optional and requires a separately installed **local** Python Docling
147: CLI and prefetched layout/table models. Electron installers do not gain this Python runtime or
148: model assets merely by bundling JavaScript. Packaging must include architecture-compatible Python,
149: Docling/PyTorch dependencies and model artifacts outside the ASAR, or document a local installation.
150: No manifests or installer definitions are changed by this slice.
151: 
152: Example development preparation (an explicit operator action, never an automatic document fallback):
153: 
154: ```sh
155: python -m venv .venv-docling
156: # Activate this environment using your platform's normal command.
157: python -m pip install docling
158: docling-tools models download layout tableformer
159: # Set DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH to an absolute path containing these prefetched artifacts.
160: # On Windows, pass the trusted .venv-docling/Scripts/docling.exe path as doclingCommand.
161: # On macOS/Linux, pass the trusted .venv-docling/bin/docling path as doclingCommand.
162: docling --help
163: ```
164: 
165: Pin and test the chosen Python/Docling/PyTorch versions when packaging. Intel macOS has distinct
166: PyTorch compatibility constraints described in the official installation page. Prefetch happens
167: before sensitive document parsing and may contact model repositories; parsing itself never installs
168: dependencies or downloads assets.
169: 
170: The reader probes help locally (at most two five-second subprocesses), detects the newer `convert`
171: subcommand versus a compatible legacy CLI, and checks required safety/page/export flags. A missing
172: executable, unsupported CLI, or absent absolute `DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH` leaves TXT/XLSX available and
173: reports complex formats unsupported. A help probe does not prove that every required model is
174: installed; missing/incompatible model assets produce an explicit conversion error.
175: 
176: Conversion uses `spawn` with an argument array and `shell: false`, a private temporary directory,
177: a fixed temporary input filename, JSON output, `--page-range 1-N`, a 120-second CLI/process timeout,
178: abort-signal cancellation, and bounded subprocess/output bytes. The subprocess receives only an
179: allowlisted local environment, not provider credentials. Remote services and external plugins are
180: disabled, model-cache offline flags are set, and OCR is disabled in this deliberately narrow slice.
181: Scanned PDFs need a separately approved local OCR integration; no cloud OCR fallback exists. The
182: runtime must be provisioned offline and can additionally be network-sandboxed by packaging policy.
183: 
184: PDF/PPTX page limits are passed to the backend. DOCX does not have stable PDF-style pagination;
185: records state that bounds apply where supported and do not claim complete page coverage. Exported
186: text prefers Docling `orig` over normalized `text`, tables retain cell spans/flags, footnote refs and
187: original text, and records retain JSON pointers/page provenance plus the original imported artifact
188: ID. Temporary files are removed in `finally`, including on cancellation; cleanup failure is explicit.
189: 
190: The current development host has no detected `docling` command. Tests exercise deterministic
191: TXT/XLSX ingestion and a **synthetic local executable** for real subprocess invocation, safety flags,
192: JSON export ingestion and cancellation. They do not claim a real Python/model-backed PDF conversion
193: was run or that Docling is already packaged.
</content>

20:

22: export const WorkflowEdge = z.object({
23:   id: z.string().min(1),
24:   source: z.string().min(1),
25:   sourcePort: z.string().min(1),
26:   target: z.string().min(1),
27:   targetPort: z.string().min(1),
28: });
29: export type WorkflowEdge = z.infer<typeof WorkflowEdge>;
30: 
31: /** One workplace: the top level of a workflow, or the inside of an expandable block. */
32: export interface WorkflowGraph {
33:   blocks: WorkflowBlock[];
34:   edges: WorkflowEdge[];
35: }
36: 
37: export const BlockId = z.string().regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,99}$/);
38: 
39: export const WorkflowBlock: z.ZodType<WorkflowBlock> = z.object({
40:   id: BlockId,
41:   kind: BlockKind,
42:   label: z.string().trim().min(1).max(80),
43:   position: z.object({ x: z.number(), y: z.number() }),
44:   params: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()),
45:   get inner() {
46:     return WorkflowGraph.optional();
47:   },
48: });
49: 
50: /** Shape only. `validateGraph` (graph.ts) checks ports, params, cycles and unique ids. */
51: export const WorkflowGraph = z.object({
52:   blocks: z.array(WorkflowBlock),
53:   edges: z.array(WorkflowEdge),
54: });
55: 
56: export const Workflow = WorkflowGraph.extend({
57:   id: z.string().startsWith("wf_"),
58:   name: z.string().min(1),
59:   description: z.string().optional(),
60:   scope: ProductScope,
61:   version: z.number().int().positive(), // +1 on every save
62:   createdAt: z.iso.datetime(),
63:   updatedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
64: });
65: export type Workflow = z.infer<typeof Workflow>;
66: 
67: export const RunStatus = z.enum([
68:   "queued",
69:   "running",
70:   "waiting_for_review", // paused at a HIL block until a person has reviewed
71:   "completed",
72:   "failed",
73:   "cancelled",
74: ]);
75: export type RunStatus = z.infer<typeof RunStatus>;
76: 
77: export const BlockRunStatus = z.enum([
78:   "pending",
79:   "running",
80:   "succeeded",
81:   "failed",
82:   "skipped", // an upstream block failed
83:   "waiting_for_review",
84: ]);
85: export type BlockRunStatus = z.infer<typeof BlockRunStatus>;
86: 
87: export const BlockRunLog = z.object({ at: z.iso.datetime(), message: z.string() });
88: export type BlockRunLog = z.infer<typeof BlockRunLog>;
89: 
90: /** Status shown on each block. Full block output is stored separately (see ARCHITECTURE.md). */
91: export const BlockRun = z.object({
92:   blockId: BlockId, // ids are unique across inner workplaces too
93:   status: BlockRunStatus,
94:   startedAt: z.iso.datetime().optional(),
95:   finishedAt: z.iso.datetime().optional(),
96:   progress: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(),
97:   counts: z.partialRecord(DataKey, z.number().int().nonnegative()), // output size per data key
98:   logs: z.array(BlockRunLog),
99:   error: z.string().optional(),
100: });
101: export type BlockRun = z.infer<typeof BlockRun>;
102: 
103: export const WorkflowRun = z.object({
104:   id: z.string().startsWith("run_"),
105:   workflowId: z.string().startsWith("wf_"),
106:   workflowVersion: z.number().int().positive(),
107:   graph: WorkflowGraph, // snapshot, so a run stays reproducible after the workflow is edited
108:   scope: ProductScope,
109:   status: RunStatus,
110:   startedBy: Actor,
111:   startedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
112:   finishedAt: z.iso.datetime().optional(),
113:   blockRuns: z.array(BlockRun),
114:   error: z.string().optional(),
115: });
116: export type WorkflowRun = z.infer<typeof WorkflowRun>;
117:

119: export interface WorkflowTemplate {

121:   description: string;
122:   graph: WorkflowGraph;
123: }

4: 
5: /** Throw this from a handler to send a specific error code to the UI. */
6: export class ReqflowError extends Error {
7:   constructor(
8:     readonly code: string,
9:     message: string,
10:     readonly details?: unknown,
11:   ) {
12:     super(message);
13:     this.name = "ReqflowError";
14:   }
15: }
16: 
17: export function toIpcError(err: unknown): ApiError["error"] {
18:   if (err instanceof ReqflowError) {
19:     return { code: err.code, message: err.message, details: err.details };
20:   }
21:   if (err instanceof ZodError) {
22:     return { code: "invalid_input", message: "Input failed validation", details: err.issues };
23:   }
24:   return { code: "internal", message: "Internal operation failed. Sensitive error details are not exposed." };
25: }
26: 
27: /** Pure (Electron-free) so it can be unit-tested: route one IPC call to its handler. */
28: export async function dispatch(
29:   handlers: ReqflowHandlers,
30:   namespace: string,
31:   method: string,
32:   args: unknown[],
33: ): Promise<IpcResult<unknown>> {
34:   const ns = (handlers as unknown as Record<string, Record<string, unknown> | undefined>)[
35:     namespace
36:   ];
37:   const fn = ns?.[method];
38:   if (typeof fn !== "function") {
39:     return {
40:       ok: false,
41:       error: { code: "unknown_method", message: `No handler for ${namespace}.${method}` },
42:     };
43:   }
44:   try {
45:     return { ok: true, value: await fn.apply(ns, args) };
46:   } catch (err) {

## Findings

1. **Severity: major**  
   **Location:** `apps/desktop/src/main/research/secrets.ts:20`  
   **Issue:** `z.record(SecretName, ...)` requires **every enum key** in Zod 4, but `set()` persists only configured credentials. Saving one credential—or removing the last one—makes the next startup fail. Both cases reproduced with synthetic storage.  
   **Suggestion:** Use `z.partialRecord(SecretName, ...)`. Add save → reload → remove → reload coverage.

2. **Severity: major**  
   **Location:** `apps/desktop/src/main/research/storage.ts:38–40`  
   **Issue:** Audit appends read outside the write queue: `existing = await this.read(...)`, then `await this.write(...existing, event)`. Concurrent operations read the same history and overwrite each other. Two synthetic concurrent appends retained only one event.  
   **Suggestion:** Serialize the **entire read-modify-write operation**, or use append-only persistence.

3. **Severity: major**  
   **Location:** `apps/desktop/src/main/research/runtime.ts:136–138, 62–109`  
   **Issue:** The busy check precedes `await store.saveState()` and audit persistence; job registration happens afterward. Two concurrent `runs.start(workflowId)` calls both succeeded, creating separate runs. `launch()` likewise awaits dataset loading between `jobs.has(input.id)` and `jobs.set(...)`, leaving a resume race.  
   **Suggestion:** Reserve workflow/run execution synchronously before the first await; release reservations on failure.

4. **Severity: major**  
   **Location:** `packages/blocks/src/research/export.ts:5–19`  
   **Issue:** The exporter reads `metadata.sourceClassifications` and `metadata.originalFields`, while the importer writes `sourceAssociations`, `vfcAssociations`, and `classifications` (`documents/local.ts:278–279, 339–341`). A synthetic import with one opinion and two VFC associations exported one feedback row with blank Brand, Feedback Type, and VFC columns. This is distinct from length/formula handling.  
   **Suggestion:** Map each preserved association’s `headers`/`values` into export columns, retaining one opinion ID across association rows.

5. **Severity: major**  
   **Location:** `packages/blocks/src/research/raw.ts:49–58`  
   **Issue:** `sources.set(source.id, source)` and `records.set(record.id, { ...record, ... })` select the **last argument**, not the latest collected revision. An older dataset supplied last replaces newer evidence while the limitation claims “latest collected revision.” The existing reverse-order revision test fails.  
   **Suggestion:** Select source/record content by `retrievedAt`, independently unioning agent/run provenance and limitations.

6. **Severity: major**  
   **Location:** `packages/blocks/src/research/runtime.ts:57–59`  
   **Issue:** Provider selection only distinguishes Tavily: `...provider === "tavily" ? "tavily" : originalProvider`. Consequently, Web research **Off** still invokes enabled Firecrawl; `anthropic_web_search` also silently selects Firecrawl. The Off case reproduced with a synthetic adapter.  
   **Suggestion:** Handle every configured provider explicitly: Off suppresses web search; unsupported Claude search returns a clear limitation rather than substituting another provider.

7. **Severity: minor**  
   **Location:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/settings/sections/ResearchApisSection.helpers.ts:275–278`  
   **Issue:** `await reloadSettings()` invokes a whole-store load, which does `set({ settings: stored, ... })` (`lib/settings-store.ts:70–71`). This erases unrelated edits awaiting the 400-ms autosave. A synthetic theme edit followed by provider configuration reverted to the old theme and then saved it.  
   **Suggestion:** Reconcile only authoritative `research.apis` values into the local store, preserving pending edits elsewhere.

147: function providerScope(
148:   scope: ResearchScope,

152:   if (provider === "local_documents") return scope;

155:     ? scope.allowedDomains.length
156:       ? intersectDomains(scope.allowedDomains, platform)
157:       : platform
158:     : scope.allowedDomains;
159:   if (
160:     (platform.length && !allowedDomains.length) ||
161:     (allowedDomains.length &&
162:       allowedDomains.every((host) =>
163:         scope.blockedDomains.some((blocked) => matchesHost(host, blocked)),
164:       ))

167:   return { ...scope, allowedDomains };

171:   // Imported originals are not public network sources. Their identity is checked by the local adapter.
172:   if (item.provider === "local_documents")

210: export function createResearchCollector(options: ResearchCollectorOptions): ResearchCollector {
211:   return {
212:     async collect(input, context) {
213:       const request = ResearchRequest.parse(input);
214:       const signal = AbortSignal.any([
215:         context.signal,
216:         AbortSignal.timeout(request.limits.timeoutMs),
217:       ]);
218:       const budget = { used: 0 };
219:       const httpOptions = { limits: request.limits, signal, fetchImpl: options.fetchImpl, budget };
220:       const http = createProviderHttp(httpOptions);
221:       const adapters = options.adapters ?? createResearchAdapters();
222:       const secrets = Object.values(options.credentials).filter(
223:         (value): value is string => !!value,
224:       );
225:       const safe = (message: string) => redactSecrets(message, secrets);
226:       const parts: ResearchDataset[] = [];
227:       const uniqueRecords = new Set<string>();
228:       let plannerRequests = 0;
229:       let planner: ReturnType<typeof createMastraQueryPlanner> | undefined;

232:         (context as typeof context & { planQueries?: boolean }).planQueries ??
233:         options.queryPlanning ??
234:         false;
235:       const canPlan =
236:         planQueries === true &&
237:         options.settings.llm.provider === "anthropic" &&
238:         !!options.credentials.anthropic_api_key?.trim() &&
239:         !!options.settings.llm.fastModel?.trim();

241:       let policyError: string | undefined;
242:       try {
243:         scope = { ...scope, ...mergeResearchDomainPolicy(options.settings.research, scope) };
244:       } catch (error) {

247:         );
248:       }
249:       const agents = [...new Set(request.agents)];

251:       for (const [index, agentId] of agents.entries()) {
252:         const definition = RESEARCH_AGENTS.find((entry) => entry.id === agentId)!;
253:         const limitations: string[] = [];
254:         const sources: Source[] = [];
255:         const records: ResearchRecord[] = [];
256:         const states: CollectionStatus[] = [];
257:         const startRequests = http.requests + plannerRequests;
258:         const eligible: {
259:           provider: ResearchProviderId;
260:           adapter: ProviderAdapter;
261:           scope: ResearchScope;
262:           config: ResearchProviderConfig;
263:         }[] = [];
264:         const note = (status: CollectionStatus, message: string) => {
265:           states.push(status);
266:           limitations.push(safe(message));
267:         };
268: 
269:         if (signal.aborted) note("cancelled", "Research cancelled or time limit reached.");
270:         else
271:           for (const originalProvider of definition.providers) {
272:             let provider = originalProvider;
273:             if (originalProvider === "firecrawl") {
274:               const selected = options.settings.research.provider;
275:               if (selected === "off") {
276:                 note(
277:                   "blocked",
278:                   "Web research is off; Firecrawl and Tavily collection are disabled.",
279:                 );
280:                 continue;
281:               }
282:               if (selected === "anthropic_web_search") {
283:                 note(
284:                   "blocked",
285:                   "anthropic_web_search is unsupported for raw original collection; explicitly select Firecrawl or Tavily.",
286:                 );
287:                 continue;
288:               }
289:               provider = selected;
290:             }
291:             const config = options.settings.research.apis[provider];
292:             if (!config.enabled) {
293:               note("blocked", `${provider}: disabled in Research APIs Settings.`);
294:               continue;
295:             }
296:             if ((provider === "reddit" || provider === "apify") && config.approval !== "granted") {
297:               note("blocked", `${provider}: usage approval not granted.`);
298:               continue;
299:             }
300:             const actorError = actorGate(agentId, provider, config);
301:             if (actorError) {
302:               note("blocked", actorError);
303:               continue;
304:             }
305:             if (
306:               provider !== "openalex" &&
307:               PROVIDER_SECRETS[provider].some((name) => !options.credentials[name]?.trim())
308:             ) {
309:               note("missing_credentials", `${provider}: required credentials are missing.`);
310:               continue;
311:             }
312:             const adapter = adapters.get(provider);
313:             if (!adapter) {
314:               note("blocked", `${provider}: adapter not installed.`);
315:               continue;
316:             }
317:             if (policyError && provider !== "local_documents") {
318:               note("blocked", `${provider}: ${policyError}`);
319:               continue;
320:             }
321:             let restricted: ResearchScope;
322:             try {
323:               restricted = providerScope(scope, agentId, provider);
324:             } catch {
325:               note(
326:                 "blocked",
327:                 `${provider}: source platform is excluded by the research domain policy.`,
328:               );
329:               continue;
330:             }
331:             if (uniqueRecords.size >= request.limits.maxResults) {
332:               note("partial", "Shared result limit reached.");
333:               continue;
334:             }
335:             if (provider !== "local_documents" && budget.used >= request.limits.maxRequests) {
336:               note("partial", "Shared request budget exhausted.");
337:               continue;
338:             }
339:             eligible.push({ provider, adapter, scope: restricted, config });
340:           }
341: 
342:         let queries: string[] = [];
343:         let queryError = false;
344:         const queryWork = eligible.some(({ provider }) => usesQueries(provider));
345:         if (queryWork) {
346:           try {
347:             queries = buildQueries(agentId, scope);
348:           } catch {
349:             queryError = true;
350:             note(
351:               "error",
352:               "Invalid deterministic research query scope; no queries or results fabricated.",
353:             );
354:           }
355:           // Reserve at least one request for collection. Explicit URL-only Apify work does not use queries.
356:           const planningWork = eligible.some(
357:             ({ provider }) =>
358:               usesQueries(provider) &&
359:               !(provider === "apify" && (agentId === "instagram" || scope.urls.length > 0)),
360:           );
361:           if (
362:             !queryError &&
363:             canPlan &&
364:             planningWork &&
365:             budget.used + 1 < request.limits.maxRequests
366:           ) {
367:             try {
368:               signal.throwIfAborted();
369:               planner ??= createMastraQueryPlanner({
370:                 apiKey: options.credentials.anthropic_api_key!,
371:                 modelId: options.settings.llm.fastModel,
372:               });
373:               budget.used += 1;
374:               plannerRequests += 1;
375:               queries = await withAbort(planner(agentId, scope, signal), signal);
376:             } catch {
377:               queryError = true;
378:               note(
379:                 signal.aborted ? "cancelled" : "error",
380:                 signal.aborted
381:                   ? "Research cancelled or time limit reached."
382:                   : "Mastra query planning failed; no deterministic fallback, fabricated queries or results used.",
383:               );
384:             }
385:           }
386:         }
387: 
388:         for (const { provider, adapter, scope: restricted, config } of eligible) {
389:           if (queryError && usesQueries(provider)) continue;
390:           if (signal.aborted) {
391:             note("cancelled", "Research cancelled or time limit reached.");
392:             break;
393:           }
394:           const remaining = request.limits.maxResults - uniqueRecords.size;
395:           if (remaining <= 0) {
396:             note("partial", "Shared result limit reached.");
397:             break;
398:           }
399:           if (provider !== "local_documents" && budget.used >= request.limits.maxRequests) {
400:             note("partial", "Shared request budget exhausted.");
401:             continue;
402:           }
403:           try {
404:             const outcome = await adapter.collect(
405:               { agentId, scope: restricted, queries },
406:               {
407:                 http,
408:                 credentials: options.credentials,
409:                 config,
410:                 limits: {
411:                   ...request.limits,
412:                   maxResults: remaining,
413:                   maxRequests: Math.max(1, request.limits.maxRequests - plannerRequests),
414:                 },
415:                 signal,
416:                 log: (message) => context.log(safe(message)),
417:                 now: () => new Date().toISOString(),
418:                 documents: options.documents,
419:               },
420:             );
421:             states.push(outcome.status);
422:             limitations.push(...outcome.limitations.map(safe));
423:             // Inspect all returned records: duplicates do not consume unique result slots.
424:             for (const value of outcome.items) {
425:               try {
426:                 const item = CollectedItem.parse(value);
427:                 if (item.provider !== provider || !allowedSource(item, restricted)) {
428:                   note(
429:                     "partial",
430:                     `${provider}: returned source excluded by the provider or public-source domain policy.`,
431:                   );
432:                   continue;
433:                 }
434:                 const { source, record } = normalizeItem(
435:                   item,
436:                   agentId,
437:                   context.runId,
438:                   new Date().toISOString(),
439:                 );
440:                 if (
441:                   !uniqueRecords.has(record.id) &&
442:                   uniqueRecords.size >= request.limits.maxResults
443:                 ) {
444:                   note(
445:                     "partial",
446:                     "Shared result limit reached; excess unique records were not retained.",
447:                   );
448:                   continue;
449:                 }
450:                 uniqueRecords.add(record.id);
451:                 sources.push(source);
452:                 records.push(record);
453:               } catch {
454:                 note(
455:                   "error",
456:                   `${provider}: malformed original record was skipped; previously collected originals were retained.`,
457:                 );
458:               }
459:             }
460:           } catch (error) {
461:             const failure = errorReport(error);
462:             note(
463:               signal.aborted || failure.code === "cancelled"
464:                 ? "cancelled"
465:                 : failure.code === "invalid_credentials"
466:                   ? "missing_credentials"
467:                   : failure.code === "permission_required" || failure.code === "unsupported"
468:                     ? "blocked"
469:                     : "error",
470:               `${provider}: ${failure.message}`,
471:             );
472:           }
473:         }
474:         const status: AgentCollectionResult["status"] =
475:           signal.aborted || states.includes("cancelled")
476:             ? "cancelled"
477:             : records.length
478:               ? states.some((state) => state !== "success" && state !== "empty")
479:                 ? "partial"
480:                 : "success"
481:               : states.includes("error")
482:                 ? "error"
483:                 : states.includes("missing_credentials")
484:                   ? "missing_credentials"
485:                   : states.includes("blocked")
486:                     ? "blocked"
487:                     : states.includes("partial")
488:                       ? "partial"
489:                       : "empty";
490:         const result: AgentCollectionResult = {
491:           agentId,
492:           status,
493:           recordIds: [...new Set(records.map((record) => record.id))],
494:           limitations: [...new Set(limitations)],
495:           requests: http.requests + plannerRequests - startRequests,
496:         };
497:         parts.push(
498:           ResearchDataset.parse({
499:             schemaVersion: 1,
500:             runId: context.runId,
501:             sources,
502:             records,
503:             results: [result],
504:             retrievedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
505:             synthetic: false,
506:           }),
507:         );
508:         await options.save(mergeResearchDatasets(...parts));
509:         context.log(`${definition.label}: ${status}, ${result.recordIds.length} original records.`);
510:         for (const limitation of result.limitations)
511:           context.log(`${definition.label}: ${limitation}`);
512:         context.progress((index + 1) / agents.length);
513:       }
514:       return mergeResearchDatasets(...parts);
515:     },
516:   };
517: }

Translate acceptance conditions into smallest sufficient proof set.

- Reuse still-current results with matching repository state.

Stop immediately when acceptance proof is complete. Report commands, results, and unresolved risk only.

5: /**
6:  * Where the settings live, as far as the UI knows:
7:  * - "loading": asking the main process
8:  * - "saved": loaded from / saved to disk
9:  * - "unavailable": main has no settings storage yet (WS1) — changes apply until the app restarts
10:  * - "error": loading or saving failed; `error` says why
11:  */
12: export type SettingsPersistence = "loading" | "saved" | "unavailable" | "error";
13: 
14: export interface SettingsState {
15:   settings: Settings;
16:   persistence: SettingsPersistence;
17:   error: string | null;
18:   /** Ask main for the stored settings. Keeps the defaults when storage isn't built yet. */
19:   load(): Promise<void>;
20:   /** Refresh only main-owned provider APIs. Keeps local edits, persistence state and pending autosave. */
21:   reloadResearchApis(): Promise<void>;
22:   /**
23:    * Merge `patch` into one section, validated with the `Settings` schema. Returns a readable
24:    * error and changes nothing when invalid; otherwise applies it and saves in the background.
25:    */
26:   update<K extends keyof Settings>(section: K, patch: Partial<Settings[K]>): string | null;
27:   resetSection(section: keyof Settings): void;
28: }
29: 
30: const SAVE_DELAY_MS = 400;
31: 
32: export function createSettingsStore(client: Pick<ReqflowApi, "settings">) {
33:   let saveTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
34:   let localRevision = 0;
35:   let saveGeneration = 0;
36:   let researchReloadGeneration = 0;
37:   let researchApisRevision = 0;
38: 
39:   return createStore<SettingsState>()((set, get) => {
40:     const save = () => {
41:       clearTimeout(saveTimer);
42:       saveTimer = setTimeout(async () => {
43:         if (get().persistence === "unavailable") return;
44:         const revision = localRevision;
45:         const generation = ++saveGeneration;
46:         const apisRevision = researchApisRevision;
47:         const current = () => revision === localRevision && generation === saveGeneration;
48:         try {
49:           const response = await client.settings.save(get().settings);
50:           if (!current()) return;
51:           const saved = Settings.parse(response);
52:           // A configure/reload may finish while this full-settings save is in flight.
53:           // Its earlier response cannot undo the provider access state just reconciled.
54:           if (apisRevision !== researchApisRevision) {
55:             saved.research.apis = get().settings.research.apis;
56:           }
57:           set({ settings: saved, persistence: "saved", error: null });
58:         } catch (err) {
59:           if (!current()) return;
60:           if (err instanceof ReqflowError && err.code === "not_implemented") {
61:             set({ persistence: "unavailable", error: null });
62:           } else {
63:             set({ persistence: "error", error: errorMessage(err, "Saving settings failed") });
64:           }
65:         }
66:       }, SAVE_DELAY_MS);
67:     };
68: 
69:     const apply = <K extends keyof Settings>(section: K, value: Settings[K]): string | null => {
70:       const parsed = Settings.shape[section].safeParse(value);
71:       if (!parsed.success) {
72:         const issue = parsed.error.issues[0];
73:         return issue ? issue.message : "Invalid value";
74:       }
75:       localRevision++;
76:       set({ settings: { ...get().settings, [section]: parsed.data } });
77:       save();
78:       return null;
79:     };
80: 
81:     return {
82:       settings: DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
83:       persistence: "loading",
84:       error: null,
85: 
86:       async load() {
87:         set({ persistence: "loading", error: null });
88:         try {
89:           const stored = Settings.parse(await client.settings.get());
90:           set({ settings: stored, persistence: "saved" });
91:         } catch (err) {
92:           if (err instanceof ReqflowError && err.code === "not_implemented") {
93:             set({ persistence: "unavailable" });
94:           } else {
95:             set({ persistence: "error", error: errorMessage(err, "Loading settings failed") });
96:           }
97:         }
98:       },
99: 
100:       async reloadResearchApis() {
101:         const generation = ++researchReloadGeneration;
102:         researchApisRevision++;
103:         try {
104:           const response = await client.settings.get();
105:           if (generation !== researchReloadGeneration) return;
106:           const stored = Settings.parse(response);
107:           researchApisRevision++;
108:           const settings = get().settings;
109:           set({
110:             settings: {
111:               ...settings,
112:               research: { ...settings.research, apis: stored.research.apis },
113:             },
114:           });
115:         } catch (err) {
116:           if (generation === researchReloadGeneration) throw err;
117:         }
118:       },
119: 
120:       update(section, patch) {
121:         return apply(section, { ...get().settings[section], ...patch });
122:       },
123: 
124:       resetSection(section) {
125:         apply(section, DEFAULT_SETTINGS[section]);
126:       },
127:     };
128:   });
129: }

131: function errorMessage(err: unknown, fallback: string): string {
132:   return err instanceof Error && err.message ? `${fallback}: ${err.message}` : fallback;
133: }

18: export async function startEditorWorkflow(

23:   onSaved?: (workflow: Workflow) => void,

29:   const workflow = await client.workflows.save({
30:     ...(workflowId ? { id: workflowId } : {}),

33:     ...structuredClone(graph),
34:   });

39: const settled = new Set(["completed", "failed", "cancelled", "waiting_for_review"]);
40: export function isRunBusy(run: WorkflowRun | null): boolean {
41:   return (
42:     !!run &&
43:     (run.status === "queued" || run.status === "running" || run.status === "waiting_for_review")
44:   );
45: }

47: /** Main can push completion before start/cancel returns its older snapshot. */
48: export function reconcileRun(current: WorkflowRun | null, next: WorkflowRun): WorkflowRun {
49:   if (
50:     current?.id === next.id &&
51:     settled.has(current.status) &&
52:     (next.status === "queued" || next.status === "running")
53:   )
54:     return current;
55:   return next;

64:     case "empty":
